nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis of gradient NiFe-LDH
nodes.procedure: NiFe-LDH nanoarrays grown on Ni foam by one-step hydrothermal method [20]: Ni foam substrate with Ni(NO3)2·6H2O, Fe(NO3)3·9H2O precursors and urea; Fe3+ partially oxidizes Ni foam creating Ni2-δ; sequential nucleation forms Ni-rich bottom (Ni:Fe 3.5:1, low Ksp) then Fe-rich top (Ni:Fe 2.4:1, high pH from urea hydrolysis).
nodes.source_text: The Nanoarray-LDH were prepared by a simple hydrothermal method [20]... NiFe-LDH grown on Ni foam prepared via one-step hydrothermal method was refocused.

unit_operations.name: Ni-rich LDH nucleation
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: Fe3+, Ni2+ with low Ksp nucleate forming Ni2-δ-O-Ni2+-O-Fe3+ moiety

unit_operations.name: Fe-rich epitaxial growth
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: Fe3-δ and Ni2-δ with high Ksp sediment forming Fe-rich top structure

nodes.name: Co-precipitation synthesis of colloidal NiFe-LDH
nodes.procedure: Colloidal NiFe-LDH nanosheets were prepared by co-precipitation method where Ni2+ and Fe3+ nucleate simultaneously forming uniform gradient-free NiFe-LDH with Ni:Fe ratio 3.42:1 close to feeding ratio.
nodes.source_text: Colloidal-LDH nanosheets prepared by co-precipitation method was used as counterparts [21]... Ni2+ and Fe3+ will nucleate simultaneously

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS O 1s spectra show M-O bonds at 529.8 eV and increased intensity of adsorbed O-O at 532.8 eV in gradient NiFe-LDH, suggesting enhanced binding strength to oxygenated intermediates.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Fig. 2a, the binding strength of NiFe-LDH with/without gradient composition to oxygenated intermediates is revealed by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) O 1s spectra. The O species at 529.8 eV are assignable to the typical metal-oxygen (M − O) bonds in NiFe-LDH. ... However, there observes an obvious increase in intensity of adsorbed O-O in NiFe-LDH after gradient Fe doping, suggesting enhanced binding strength of gradient NiFe-LDH surface to oxygenated intermediates.
